sentences.text:
Naveen Baid @ Naviin Baid vs Union Of India & Anr on 11
August, 2023
Author: Bibek Chaudhuri

Bench: Bibek Chaudhuri
11.08.2023
 Sl. No.10.
 Mithun
 Ct.No.42.
 Wpa 18143 of 2023
 Naveen Baid @ Naviin Baid
 Vs.
 Union of India & Anr.
 Mr. Ayan Banerjee,
 Mr. Anirban Das,
 Mr. Soumo Chaudhury,
 Mr. Suman Banerjee
 ...for the petitioner.
 Mr. Kumar Jyoti Tewari,
 ...for the respondents.

The issue involved in the instant writ petition is as to whether the petitioner can maintain an application for issuance of writ in the nature of certiorari and mandamus for violation of a statutory provision by the Government Authority when the Act contains recovery procedure through the Civil Court.
It is the case of the petitioner that the land of the petitioner was acquired by a declaratory notice under Section 10 the Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978.
However, the Metro Railways did not determine the amount payable for acquisition.
Accordingly, the petitioner moved the competent authority for determination of compensation.
Compensation was determined.
However, both the petitioner and the Metro Railways were not satisfied with the decision made by the competent authority.
Both of them preferred appeals before the Tribunal.
Tribunal disposed of both the appeals further enhancing the compensation.

At this stage, the petitioner has approached this Court alleging violation of the statutory provision of Sections13 and 14 of the said Act of 1978 as well as the purported Act by the Metro Railways taking over possession of the subject land by setting up notice board on the land.

It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Metro Railways that for enforcement of the orders of the competent authority and the appellate authority, the petitioner has the remedy of execution under the provision of Section 16C of the said Act of 1978.

Therefore, when efficacious relief is Naveen Baid @ Naviin Baid vs Union Of India & Anr on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33003174/
1 provided in the Act itself, writ remedy cannot lie.

sentences.text: The petitioner has challenged non-compliance of Section 13 and Section 14 of the said Act by the Metro Railways.

It is also the case of the petitioner that the Metro Railways is bound to fix the interest on compensation under the provision of Section 80 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: No such computation of interest has been made by the Metro Railways.
Prima facie this Court is of the view that the petitioner has been able to make out a case, which can be decided only on the basis of a report on affidavit by the respondent authorities.
Therefore, the instant writ petition is admitted.

The respondents are at liberty to file a report in the form of affidavit declaring their stand in respect of the instant writ petition within three weeks from the date of this order and serve a copy of the same to the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
The petitioner is at liberty to file exception to the report within one week thereafter.
In the meantime, the respondents are restrained from starting any construction work over the subject land till 30th September, 2023 or until further order, whichever is earlier.
In the meantime, the Metro Railway is at liberty to comply the order in accordance with Sections 13 and 14 of the 1978 Act.
On submission of compensation amount, the respondents are at liberty to continue with the possession of the land.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J.)
